experiment: Semantic Film Director 1.0 vs current storyboard — pre-registered blind A/B (preregistration-c11-director.json)
raters: AGENT raters only: 80 fresh sonnet describers (one strip each, image only), 2 x 20 fresh sonnet judges (4 descriptions of 4 different beats each, frozen answer key + narration). No human rating was collected — human reference prepared, NOT run.

wrongNotUp.value: WRONG frames A 2 -> B 4 (mean of two judge passes, 90 frames per arm)

subgroups_exploratory.note: not pre-registered as decision criteria (only the Lemo subgroup report was); n is small — read as direction, not proof
subgroups_exploratory.textOnly_H_n15: A 50 % -> B 45.6 % (-4.4 pp); ADDS 12 -> 0; 6 of B's 8 WRONG frame judgements (two passes; mean 4) came from quote cards (B05: the quote read as a concession; B09: the quote over the source scene's classroom set)

findings: The director's staged representations make the mechanism visible: EXPLAINS rose from 0.5 to 14 frames, dead frames fell from 14 to 2.5; where B staged a change, comprehension rose ~15 pp.

The director chose text-only (H) for 18 of 40 beats (15 of the 30 main beats). 12 of those 18 are beats the frozen key says state no causality; 6 had a stated cause the author did not stage. A quote card carries no picture (ADDS 0) and lost ~4 pp on average — it pulled the pooled result below the bar.

WRONG rose 2 -> 4 (mean of passes; 8 B judgements): 6 from quote cards — B05 (the quote read as a concession) and B09 (the source set behind the quote, a classroom, read as school) — and 2 from an arrow read as the wrong direction of influence (B17 values -> map). Causal arrows can be read as a mechanism the narration does not state.
Action beats did not regress (+12.5 pp): the regression guard holds.

Ceiling not reached: comprehension of both arms is under 50 % — most narration-level claims in a two-host discussion are hard to show; the answer key's own 'no causality' rate (17/40 = 43 %) bounds what any picture can explain.

authoringBias.B: 5 fresh sonnet authors, one pass + one compile-fix pass (8 contracts: 7 missing camera.purpose on H, 1 label, 1 uncausal B) — no visual iteration; the experimenter wrote the spec and the code, not a contract; 2 renderer fixes were made on SYNTHETIC contracts before any benchmark render (logged).
authoringBias.A: the shipped storyboard: authored, gated, multi-round fixed (mute tests, readcheck) per book — more authoring effort than B received.
authoringBias.direction: the budget favours A; B's gain is not explained by extra effort. A risk on the other side: the B spec was written by the experimenter who also designed the renderer; the authors were blind to the key and the rating.

deviations: audit/c11-pilots/deviations.json (render moved to GitHub Actions on the operator's order; 26 local strips + 16 local descriptions unused; decided before any rating) + ratings/repairs.log (one describer JSON missing a ']' — syntax only).

humanReference.materials: human-reference.md, human-sheet-c11.js (30 scenes, X/Y order by seeded coin), answer-key.json, rating-prompts.md
humanReference.estimatedCost: ≈ 7.5 h rater time (5 raters) + ≈ 3.5 h scoring (2 scorers)

costAndScale.authoring: ≈ 62 k sonnet tokens per 8-beat author pass (≈ 8 k per beat, mostly the spec as input); a 250-beat book ≈ 2 M tokens, minutes of wall time; compile + validation instant
costAndScale.render: SemanticStage is plain SVG + the existing rig: same CPU class as an Antidote scene; cloud stills 4 s each on GitHub runners (80 strips / 240 stills in 3 min wall on 8 runners)
costAndScale.rating: 80 describers + 40 judges ≈ 6.7 M sonnet tokens (agent session budget hit once; resumed after reset)
costAndScale.fullBookImpact: opt-in scene field; the old configs draw unchanged; production integration NOT done (NO SHIP)
